content:
Let the arithmetic sequence be  

\[
a_n = a_1+(n-1)d = 4+(n-1)d ,\qquad d\in\mathbb Z .
\]

Since the first term is \(4\) and the sequence must contain the terms \(24\) and \(34\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
4+(i-1)d &= 24 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (i-1)d = 20,\\
4+(j-1)d &= 34 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (j-1)d = 30,
\end{aligned}
\]

for some positive integers \(i,j\).  
Thus \(d\) must divide both \(20\) and \(30\); i.e.

\[
d\mid \gcd(20,30)=10 .
\]

Hence the possible integer common differences are  

\[
d\in\{1,2,5,10\}.
\]

For each such \(d\) the 10th term is

\[
a_{10}=4+9d .
\]

Compute it for each \(d\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
d=1 &: a_{10}=4+9\cdot1 = 13,\\
d=2 &: a_{10}=4+9\cdot2 = 22,\\
d=5 &: a_{10}=4+9\cdot5 = 49,\\
d=10&: a_{10}=4+9\cdot10 = 94.
\end{aligned}
\]

The sum of all these 10th terms is

\[
13+22+49+94 = 178 .
\]

\[
\boxed{178}
\]
